verdict.rationale: Skills are packaged so that Claude, the assistant they run inside, picks up and carries out tasks. Users can invoke a skill with `/skill-name` or let Claude load it when relevant. Bundled skills like `/run` and `/verify` work without setup, and skill-creator hands skill authoring itself to Claude. The assistant is really the host Claude agent rather than something Skills ships on its own, and community reports say automatic invocation is hit-or-miss (one cited eval had a skill never invoked in 56% of cases). Missing for 10: a delegation capability that belongs to Skills itself rather than the host Claude agent, reliable automatic triggering, and independent hands-on corroboration of delegated task completion.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: Claude uses skills when relevant, or you can invoke one directly with `/skill-name`.
A skill for creating new skills and iteratively improving them.
If Claude thinks the skill is relevant to the current task, it will load the skill by reading its full `SKILL.md` into context.
